setups.quote: In this section we compare the overhead cost of our fault-tolerant magic state preparation scheme for preparing an encoded |H⟩ state in the concatenated Steane code to the overhead cost of the MEK scheme for distilling |H⟩ states (also encoded in the concatenated Steane code).

We tested the decoding performance under depolarizing noise with noiseless error syndrome measurements for the rotated surface code and compared against the Blossom algorithm and a neural network based decoder.

Before we construct a surface-code implementation of the 15-to-1 protocol, we first discuss two different ways of performing faulty logical π/8 rotations with surface codes: the traditional method based on state injection, and a protocol based Accepted in Quantum 2019-10-30, click title to verify 6
From these two ingredients, we construct a decoder on the product code.
To illustrate further the advantage of augmented codes, we compare numerically the performance of toric codes and their product with a [[4, 2, 2]] code.
In Figure 3, we compare the product TC(m) ⊗ [[4, 2, 2]] with all the toric codes TC(l) achieving a smaller or equal qubit overhead.
